# Kavros — the governance plane for enterprise AI

> Kavros is a self-hosted governance plane that sits at the enforcement
> boundary for AI agents, employee AI chat, and scheduled AI workflows:
> Ed25519-signed policies enforced inside an AWS Nitro Enclave, DLP
> inspection before egress, a boundary-enforced kill switch, and a
> hash-chained, attestation-backed evidence trail. Deployed in the
> customer's own VPC on their own AWS account. kavros.ai · docs.kavros.ai

## What Kavros enforces

- **Signed policies:** every workload runs under an Ed25519-signed runtime
  policy (approved targets, data surfaces, limits) verified inside the
  enclave before enforcement. Unsigned or tampered policies are rejected.
- **DLP before egress:** content is inspected — and blocked or redacted —
  before anything reaches the model, target API, artifact, or email.
- **Kill switch:** halting a workload is enforced at the data-plane
  boundary (not in the application), takes effect immediately, quotes the
  operator's stated reason, and is fully audited.
- **Evidence:** every allowed/blocked decision lands in a hash-chained
  audit trail and can carry a Nitro attestation document chaining to the
  release-built enclave image. Exports are designed for SOC 2 / ISO 42001 /
  EU AI Act evidence programs.
- **Surfaces covered:** autonomous agents, employee AI chat (BYOK, prompts
  inspected before the model sees them), and scheduled AI workflows (signed
  revisions, column-level scopes, governed destinations).

## What Kavros does NOT claim

- Attestation proves *which code and which policy* made a decision — not
  that the policy is correct or the agent is safe.
- Kavros produces evidence; it does not make anyone compliant.
- Failover behavior differs by deployment tier (Business is
  single-instance by design).
- Nothing leaves the deployment except through an inspected, approved,
  metered, evidenced path — "no data ever leaves" would be false.

## Pages

- [Home](https://kavros.ai/): product overview, surfaces, pricing
  (Business $2,500/mo, Enterprise $7,500/mo, Regulated from $18,000/mo),
  paid 15-business-day proof offer.
- [Interactive sandbox](https://kavros.ai/sandbox.html): runnable attack
  scenarios (agent halt, chat DLP leak, workflow drift) with recorded
  product videos.
- [Security](https://kavros.ai/security.html): architecture, enforcement
  boundary, chat privacy model, shared security responsibilities.
- [Privacy](https://kavros.ai/privacy.html): privacy model for the website,
  employee chat, and customer deployments.
- [Blog](https://kavros.ai/blog.html): technical deep dives on agent
  security and prompt injection.
- [Can you prove what your AI agent touched?](https://kavros.ai/prove-what-your-agent-touched.html):
  the launch technical brief — the four questions security reviews ask,
  the propose→approve→sign→enforce→meter→prove chain, and an explicit
  claims/non-claims section.
- [CVE-2026-21852 case study](https://kavros.ai/cve-2026-21852.html):
  how Cursor's agent mode was compromised via prompt injection, why
  traditional security controls miss it (the lethal trifecta), and the
  architectural shift required to stop it.
- [Documentation](https://docs.kavros.ai): deployment, integration (HTTP
  contract, CLI, Python hook), policy model, evidence exports.
